diagnostics.message: Unused code check skipped: Knip is not set up in this project
diagnostics.help: Unused files, exports and dependencies were not checked. Add a knip config file (for example knip.json) or add knip to devDependencies to enable the check, or set quality.knip: always to run it without that setup.

scoreImpact.rationale: A skipped unused code check is visibility loss, not evidence of dead code.

diagnostics.help: Remove unused imports to keep the code clean

diagnostics.message: Mutable default argument `links=[]`. The default is shared across all calls — bugs that look like state-leakage.
diagnostics.help: Use `None` as the default and create the mutable value inside the body: `def f(items=None): items = items if items is not None else []`. Standard Python idiom; anything else is the AI agent shortcutting.

scoreImpact.rationale: Mutable defaults are a high-confidence Python behavior bug.

diagnostics.message: `range(len(doc))` loop — usually a hand-rolled iteration pattern.
diagnostics.help: Prefer direct iteration (`for item in items`) or `enumerate(items)` when the index is needed. Keeping index plumbing out of the loop reduces checkpoint-to-checkpoint bloat.

scoreImpact.rationale: Index loops are style/readability signals and often not harmful.

diagnostics.help: Normalize the input at the boundary, use a typed object, or split the lookup into explicit steps. Empty-dict fallback chains are a common agent shortcut that becomes brittle as schemas evolve.

scoreImpact.rationale: Chained dict fallback hides shape assumptions and deserves review.

diagnostics.help: Use a table, set membership, or handler map when branches share the same shape. SlopCodeBench highlights these selector ladders as code that keeps growing instead of absorbing new cases cleanly.

scoreImpact.rationale: Repetitive dispatch ladders create maintainability debt.

scoreImpact.rationale: An unavailable audit is visibility loss, not evidence of a vulnerability.
